name: AKU-IED Accentuates Need for Leadership at School Level

content.title: AKU-IED Accentuates Need for Leadership at School Level
content.summary: A two-day conference was organised by the Aga Khan University Institute for Educational Development (AKU-IED), at the University's Karimabad campus.

media.alt: AKU-IED Accentuates Need for Leadership at School Level

content.text: A two-day conference was organised by the Aga Khan University Institute for Educational Development (AKU-IED), at the University's Karimabad campus, on March 31 and April 1, 2001. The conference, held in collaboration with the British Council Karachi, focussed on 'Creating Effective Leadership for Schools'.

Over 150 leaders from government and private schools, as well as the Aga Khan Education Service, Pakistan, gathered to share their experiences with each other. The participants included Mr Nazar Mohammad Meher, Secretary education, and Mr Anwar Ahmed Zai, Additional Secretary Education, Government of Sindh; Mr Richard Hardwick, Director British Council, and Mirza Aijaz Baig, Director of Primary Education, Hyderabad.

The objective of the leadership conference was to explore and discuss the notion of leadership and management, as a globally understood idea. It had a blend of keynote speakers from different parts of the world. Professor Tim Simkins of Sheffield Hallam University, England, spoke on leadership effectiveness in schools. The keynote address by Nadeem Mustafa Khan, Director General and CEO, the Aga Khan University Hospital, focussed on new management trends and competencies. Dr Paul Shaw of University of Toronto presented the critical issues school leaders faced in the improvement of schools.

The participants discussed issues raised in the keynote speeches and attended research seminars on different themes, ranging from school leadership and empowerment, involvement of school heads in policy decisions, to a culture of accountability in schools and encouraging research for improvement. The deliberations also provided future directions to schools, such as involvement in research and inquiry for improvement in the quality of education, development of consortium for sharing resources, experiences and practices with others, etc. It was also hoped that the school-university partnership would be strengthened through joint research projects at school level.
